appraisal_events.evidence: le petit Saint-Loup vous adorait, vous préférait même à elle
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup is reported to prefer the narrator even to his own mistress, staging the narrator as favored, though the claim reaches him third-hand (Rachel to the prince to him) and is met with the narrator's own anxious doubt, keeping the reading uncertain.

status_effects.explanation: Being told he is preferred by Saint-Loup to Rachel gives the narrator a mild boost in perceived standing within the conversation, though the mediated, layered report and his own ironic self-doubt limit how firmly this lands.

ambiguities: The praise of the narrator is triple-mediated (Saint-Loup's feeling, reported by Rachel, reported by the prince), and the narrator's own reply ('elle doit être jalouse de moi et me détester') undercuts it with anxious irony, so the positive reading is held with only moderate confidence.
